title: Consolidated Financial Statements
outcomes: Apply the scope and exemptions of Ind AS 110.
Assess power through relevant activities and rights.
Evaluate variable returns and principal-agent relationships.
Reassess control and apply the investment entity exception.

meta.exam_tip: Write the three control elements as headings and conclude on each.

concepts.title: Scope of Ind AS 110 and exemptions
body: Ind AS 110 requires a parent to present consolidated statements and sets a single control model for all investees, including structured entities.

A parent need not consolidate if: it is itself wholly owned (or partly owned with other owners informed and not objecting); its debt or equity is not publicly traded and it is not in the process of listing; and its ultimate or intermediate parent publishes Ind AS-compliant consolidated statements. Post-employment benefit plans are excluded.
Investment entities do not consolidate most subsidiaries (see later). In India, company law also determines when consolidated statements are prepared.
concepts.analogy: One control model for every type of investee.
concepts.work: An unlisted intermediate holding company may be exempt.

concepts.title: Power: relevant activities and rights
body: An investor has power when its existing rights give it the current ability to direct relevant activities — those that most significantly affect returns (e.g. operating, financing, R&D, budget decisions). Purpose and design of the investee guide the analysis.

Power usually comes from voting rights: a majority, unless another party controls via contract or the votes are not substantive. Without a majority, power can arise from contractual arrangements, rights from other agreements, de facto control (size of holding relative to dispersed others), or substantive potential voting rights (exercisable when decisions are needed and in the money or otherwise beneficial).
Protective rights (e.g. lender covenants, veto over fundamental changes) do not give power. Only substantive rights — those the holder has the practical ability to exercise — count.
concepts.analogy: Ask who directs the activities that move the returns.
concepts.work: A franchisor's brand-protection rights are protective, not power.

concepts.title: Variable returns and the link: principal or agent
body: Variable returns are returns that can vary with the investee's performance — dividends, changes in value, fees, tax benefits, residual interests, cost savings or synergies.
The link: the investor must be able to use its power to affect its own returns. A decision maker acting as agent for others does not control.

Principal vs agent factors: scope of decision-making authority; rights held by others (substantive removal rights by a single party make the manager an agent); remuneration (market-based or not); and exposure to variability from other interests. The greater the magnitude and variability of total economic interest, the more likely a principal.
concepts.analogy: Power must work for your own benefit, not just for others.
concepts.work: A manager with a fee only and removable at will is an agent.

concepts.title: Continuous assessment and investment entities
body: Control is reassessed whenever facts and circumstances indicate a change in any of the three elements — e.g. expiry of rights, new agreements, changes in market conditions that affect de facto control.

An investment entity obtains funds from investors to provide investment management services, commits to investors that its business purpose is investing solely for capital appreciation, investment income or both, and measures and evaluates performance of substantially all investments on a fair value basis.

An investment entity measures its subsidiaries at FVTPL rather than consolidating them, except subsidiaries providing investment-related services. A non-investment-entity parent of an investment entity must consolidate all its subsidiaries, including those held through the investment entity.
concepts.analogy: Keep reassessing control; investment entities fair-value their subsidiaries.
concepts.work: A venture capital fund may hold portfolio companies at fair value.

illustrations.q: Lyra Ltd. holds 45% of the votes in Vega Ltd. The remaining 55% is spread among thousands of shareholders, none holding more than 3%; there are no agreements among them, and past meetings show attendance of about 60%. Does Lyra control Vega?

illustrations.title: Is the fund manager a principal?
illustrations.q: Orion AMC manages a fund with broad decision rights. It earns a market-rate fee of 1% of assets and holds 20% of the fund units. Investors can remove Orion only by a 75% vote of independent investors. For a year where the fund (₹100 crore) gains 10%, what is Orion's total return, and is it a principal or an agent?

checks.label: Fund manager's total return per ₹100 crore of fund gain (₹ crore)

summary: Power from votes, contracts, de facto, potential votes.
traps: Equating control with majority shareholding only.

viva.q: State the three elements of control.
viva.model: Power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns, and the ability to use power to affect those returns.
Activities of the investee that significantly affect its returns, such as operating, financing and budgeting decisions.

viva.q: What makes a decision maker an agent?
viva.model: It acts mainly for others, often with limited authority, removable by others, market-based pay and small exposure to variability.
An entity that obtains funds to provide investment management, invests solely for capital appreciation or income, and evaluates substantially all investments at fair value.

viva.q: When are potential voting rights considered?
viva.model: When they are substantive — the holder has the practical ability to exercise them when decisions need to be made.

cases.title: Pegasus Ltd.
cases.case: Pegasus Ltd. owns 40% of Titan Ltd. and holds call options, currently exercisable and deep in the money, to buy another 15%. Another investor holds 35% and a bank has veto rights over borrowings above ₹100 crore. Pegasus appoints the CEO and approves the budget.

mcqs.q: Pegasus's potential voting interest including options (%):
mcqs.explain: 40 + 15 = 55 substantive. In practice: consider in assessing power.
They protect the lender. In practice: ignore for power.
Substantive options + budget and CEO rights. In practice: consolidate.

mcqs.q: If the options later expire unexercised, Pegasus must:
mcqs.explain: Change in facts triggers reassessment. In practice: may still have de facto control.
